ideas.title: Gear it down: the winch that fills up
ideas.goal: The player picks the winch's gear (1:1, 3:1, 6:1 wooden wheels) and its drum, then hauls a log, a crate or the empty cart. Fast gears snatch light loads in quickly and stall on heavy ones, slow gears haul anything but take ages. As rope piles up on the drum, the pull fades, so a long haul slows near the end. Picking the right gear for each load is the skill.
ideas.toward: The cart's drive train: the same motor, gear and drum choice decides whether the cart climbs the dune.
ideas.idea: Two pegged oak gear wheels between the motor's axle and a wider rope drum. The drum's radius is computed from the rope wound on it (r^2 = r0^2 + d^2 L / (pi W)). The tension goes back through the gear ratio into Motor.step!'s load, and the gears' tooth friction is a loss. You can see the rope coil thicken on the drum, and the log comes in fast at first, then slower.
ideas.form: Next step of the winch project (todo #790) in plugins/irondrum.jl: gear meshes that mesh visibly, a growing rope coil, gear choice in Jump in, and a traced film of a haul that slows as the drum fills.

ideas.title: Tug of war with Pickles
ideas.goal: A friend grabs the other end of the rope and digs in. The motor's torque against the creature's weight and footing decides who wins: Pickles skids across the sand on its heels, or the motor stalls, the pawl clicks and Pickles sits down hard when the switch goes off. The player picks which friend pulls and where (sand, grass, planks).
ideas.toward: Gives creatures real mass and foot friction (#745). The cart needs both for carrying friends.
ideas.idea: The rope's end ties to a creature instead of a log. The creature's mass comes from its mesh volume times a density, its grip from mu times its weight on that ground. It leans back in a pulling pose, and its feet slide when the tension beats its grip. Its footprints drag into furrows (beachprints). Nothing scripts the winner: it is tension against grip, every step.
ideas.form: A Jump in interaction by the drum (hook a friend). New pose and event kinds :tug_won / :tug_lost, and a funny dusk film of the friend being dragged.

ideas.title: Crank it backwards: the drum lights a wire
ideas.goal: The player, as Lumi, grabs the rope and runs away with it. Pulling the rope off the drum spins the motor backwards, it becomes a dynamo and a thin iron wire on the block glows dull red. Pull harder and faster and it glows brighter, and the rope gets heavier to pull because the current brakes the drum. The player feels Lenz's law in their legs.
ideas.toward: The road's 'motor run backwards: a dynamo that lights a wire', the step before the windmill charges the plates.
ideas.idea: The cells are swapped out for a load resistor (the wire). Motor.step! already has the back-EMF table, so the same drum generates E = k omega and I = E / (R_wire + R_coil). The braking torque goes back into the rope's tension, so the player's run slows. The wire's temperature comes from I^2 R minus radiation (the hot-glass glow code) and its emission colour follows its temperature.
ideas.form: Plugin change (irondrum): a 'run with the rope' control in Jump in, a glowing wire mesh with temperature-driven Emission, a traced night film of the wire flickering as Lumi runs.

ideas.title: The rope parts
ideas.goal: Hemp has a real breaking strength and wears with every haul over the block's rim. Overload it (a stuck cart, a heavy crate, a tug of war) and it parts with a whip that flings the free end across the sand. The player learns to watch the rope stretch and fray, and splices or doubles it.
ideas.toward: Real failure for the cart's tow line and the friends' safety; makes stalling a decision, not just a stop.
ideas.idea: rope.jl gets a breaking tension (6 mm hemp ~ 3 kN fresh) that falls with cumulative wear: rubbing the rim under tension, sand in the fibres. A segment whose strain passes it is cut. The two halves keep their stored elastic energy, so they snap back on their own. The drawn rope frays (radius noise and loose fibres) as wear grows.
ideas.form: Physics in rope.jl plus drawing in the plugin. Event :rope_parted, sound, and a slow-motion traced clip of the snap.

ideas.title: The pots run down
ideas.goal: Every haul costs copper salt. The blue in the six pots visibly fades and the motor gets weaker through the day, so the player chooses what is worth hauling today and when to top up the salt (made at the kiln from copper and vinegar). Tomorrow's haul depends on today's chemistry.
ideas.toward: The road's 'cells that sag': a circuit with cells that polarise and deplete, which the cart's range depends on.
ideas.idea: potcell.jl's Daniell chemistry keeps the charge actually drawn: copper ions plated per coulomb (Faraday). Concentration falls, so internal resistance rises and the limiting current drops. The pots' blue colour comes from their real Cu2+ concentration, and a bright copper crust grows on the plates.
ideas.form: Circuit and pot state saved across sessions. Pot materials change colour live, a pots panel is not needed: you see it in the liquid. A time-lapse film of the blue fading over a day of hauls.

ideas.title: A carbon brush from the campfire
ideas.goal: The player chars a willow stick in the campfire, files it to a block and swaps it in for a copper brush. Then they choose: copper hauls harder but sparks blue at every changeover, charcoal runs quiet in the dark but stalls under the log. Mixing one of each is a third answer.
ideas.toward: The brushes project. The cart needs brushes that last a whole trip without burning the commutator.
ideas.idea: Motor.commutate! (s176) already models resistance commutation. A brush's contact resistance and arc voltage come from its material: copper 0.05 Ohm / 13 V, charcoal ~1 Ohm / 20 V. Charring in the fire is a temperature-and-time process in fire.jl: a stick left too long turns to ash. Spark erosion pits the copper segments over time.
ideas.form: Campfire and drum interaction in Jump in. Brush meshes in their material (matte black char vs copper), a side-by-side traced night film of the same haul with each brush.

ideas.title: Up the lookout tree
ideas.goal: The drum hoists a basket up the lookout tree on a rope over a branch, and friends queue to ride. A light friend shoots up, a heavy one barely lifts, and the pawl holds them dangling while they wave. The player chooses who rides and where to hang the pulley.
ideas.toward: Lifting a real creature's mass on the motor; the 'friends ride along' step in a form that works before the cart does.
ideas.idea: rope.jl over a fixed sheave (friction from the wrap angle, capstan equation) to a basket body carrying a creature of real mass. The basket swings as a pendulum on its rope and the creature's pose reacts (holding on, peeking over). Nothing sets the speed: motor torque, gear, rope and mass decide it.
ideas.form: A new hoist plugin by the lookout, an event kind :basket_ride, and a film from the treetop looking down as a friend rises.

ideas.title: Lay the plank road
ideas.goal: The player carries planks from the woodpile in Lumi's beak and lays them on the dune. Each plank sinks into soft sand by its load and turns where it is laid badly. The cart hauled over them needs a twentieth of the pull it needs in sand, so where the planks go decides if the winch can get the cart up.
ideas.toward: The road's plank track and the cart's dune climb.
ideas.idea: Planks as bodies resting on sandfield.jl's soil (bearing pressure, sinkage). The wheels' rolling resistance on each surface comes from contact sinkage, not a table per surface. Planks laid end to end shift under the wheels. You see sand pushed up beside each sunk plank and ruts where there are no planks.
ideas.form: Jump in building mechanic plus soil physics, with a top-down film of the road growing plank by plank.

ideas.title: Hear the stall coming
ideas.goal: The motor's whine is synthesised every frame from its own simulation: changeover clicks at 4 per turn, ripple pitch from its speed, brush hiss from sliding. The player learns to haul by ear: the note drops as the load builds, and a stutter means it is about to stall.
ideas.toward: Makes the motor readable without a gauge, which the cart's driver will need.
ideas.idea: Real-time audio from Motor.State: each changeover's spark energy becomes a click, the torque ripple a tone at 4x the rotation frequency, and the pawl's clicks are real tooth passages. It is streamed to the browser through the voice plugin's sessions as short generated buffers every few frames, not pre-made clips.
ideas.form: Sound system change: live audio in the dashboard, and the films get the game's own sound track.

ideas.title: A sail on the axle
ideas.goal: The player fits a small sail rotor on the drum's free axle end and turns it into the wind. On a gusty day the drum spins on its own and charges the pots backwards, the blue comes back. The player trims blade angle and size against the day's wind.
ideas.toward: The road's windmill generator and 'yesterday's wind' as stored charge.
ideas.idea: Blade-element momentum on the island's wind field (wind.jl) gives the rotor torque. The drum runs as a generator into the pots, which recharge when the EMF beats the cell voltage: copper plates back out and the Cu2+ concentration rises. Too much blade stalls in light air, too little does nothing.
ideas.form: Plugin parts on the existing drum, a wind-driven event :pots_charged, and a traced film of the rotor turning in a squall with the pots' blue deepening.
